key_insight: The paper argues that for autonomous scientific discovery, the main bottleneck is no longer just agent workflows but the design of the environment that shapes agent behavior.
engineering_relevance: It reframes agent development as environment engineering—using permissions, artifacts, budgets, and human oversight to make scientific agents more reliable, efficient, and collaborative.
method: Permissioned execution with isolated evaluation to bound agent actions
Filesystem and Git-based artifact management for collaboration and traceability
Budget-aware exploration plus lightweight human-in-the-loop supervision
evidence_signal: EurekAgent reports new state-of-the-art results across multiple mathematics, kernel engineering, and machine learning tasks, including 26-circle packing with under $11 total API cost.
watch_item: The approach depends on carefully engineered environments, so results may be sensitive to implementation details and may not transfer cleanly across tasks or infrastructure.
paper_title: EurekAgent: Agent Environment Engineering is All You Need For Autonomous Scientific Discovery
